result.title: Wear and Go: Calibration Free Sparse Inertial Motion Capture via Online Sensor Setup Estimation
result.summary: Sparse inertial motion capture typically assumes that each sensor's anatomical identity and mounting orientation are known. We present MOSAIC (Motion-based Sensor Assignment and Inertial Calibration), a framework that recovers this setup from ordinary motion without a calibration pose. Our central insight is that body pose changes continuously while the sensor setup persists, allowing movements that are individually ambiguous to provide complementary evidence over time. A setup network processes unordered sensor streams with temporal and cross-sensor attention, then accumulates assignment and rotation evidence into a session-level estimate. The recovered setup canonicalizes measurements for frozen pretrained pose estimators, separating sensor configuration from motion reconstruction. For sensors worn at prescribed body sites, evaluation on real inertial recordings with randomized setups shows near-calibrated pose accuracy for bounded offsets and substantial benefits from accumulation under arbitrary orientations. Transfer across pose networks supports setup recovery as a reusable interface between interchangeable sensors and pretrained pose models.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 MOSAIC 框架，用带时序与跨传感器注意力的网络从日常动作中累积证据，估计稀疏 IMU 的传感器归属与安装朝向，从而无需标定姿态即可把测量规范化后送入冻结的姿态估计器。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「单帧歧义、跨时间累积成会话级潜变量，再将输入规范化以复用冻结模型」的思路，可能为 LVR 中把视角、传感器配置等上下文潜变量与推理状态分离、以及证据累积与置信判断提供类比线索，但领域距离较远，需核查其累积与接口设计是否可迁移。
